messages:
Sophia (PM): quick sync — Acme asked for a controlled rollout for the new priority-routing flag. they want EU-only A/B (10% user traffic) for 48h, then full if stable. need: canary, KPIs for launch, explicit fallback, and telemetry retention. who owns what?
Anna P: ok, sounds reasonable. are we doing tenant-level or user-sample AB? tenant-level for them ideally (they're a single large customer).
Jordan (Eng): tenant-level is easier for sidecars/routing. but causes capacity spike if we switch to 100% for that tenant. we should cap concurrency or use gradient ramp.
Mike (ops): capacity spike +1. we need a warmup window to spin up dedicated pods/slots. propose: 4h warmup at 0 traffic -> 10% burstable traffic -> steady 48h.
Rachel S (CS): Acme will expect a quick rollback path and a comms plan. can we guarantee <15min rollback SLA for them?
Tom (SE): rollback should be a flag flip + traffic steering to v1. but we need a tested fast path — I can add a direct route that bypasses the new code path.
Jordan (Eng): agree. rollback plan: flip flag -> if traffic drops but errors persist, revert route to model-v1. add circuit-breaker on errors >1%.
Sophia (PM): KPIs: p50/p95 latency, error rate (4xx/5xx), model-quality delta (F1 or custom metric), and cost delta per 1M tokens. retention for telemetry? they want 90d.
Mike (ops): 90d is heavy. default is 30d. for a paid enterprise customer we can do 90d as a special retention tier — need approval from billing. ops impact: +S3/ES cost estimate needed.
Anna P: also need alert thresholds: p95 latency +30% from baseline OR error rate >0.5% for 15m => auto rollback. also a manual kill switch for SRE.
DevOpsBot: Incident policy attached: https://intranet.redwood/ops/rollout-kill-switch (auto-triggers supported via /trigger-rollback).
Tom (SE): sample flag config for review:
```
flag: priority-routing-acme
scope: tenant=acme, region=eu
phases:
  - name: warmup
    duration: 4h
    traffic: 0%
  - name: canary
    duration: 48h
    traffic: 10%
    checks:
      - p95_latency < 150ms
      - error_rate < 0.5%
  - name: ramp
    duration: 2h
    traffic: 100%
fallback: route->model-v1
alerts:
  - p95_latency > baseline * 1.3 for 15m -> rollback
  - error_rate > 0.5% for 15m -> rollback
```
Rachel S (CS): that looks good. can we add an observational gate: compare quality on a set of 500 sampled prompts (eval set) every 12h? they want no regressions >2% on their critical prompts.
Jordan (Eng): we can run a shadow evaluator that runs both variants and emits a quality delta metric. overhead is small if sampled. will need the eval set from Acme.
Mike (ops): we should also set a quota guard so the tenant cannot accidentally consume more capacity than reserved during ramp. propose token_cap = 50M for the first week.
Sophia (PM): action items: (1) Jordan + Tom: implement flag + rollback path + shadow eval (due EOD tomorrow), (2) Mike: confirm warmup autoscaling and quota cap, estimate cost delta for 90d retention, (3) Rachel: request eval set + comms plan w/ Acme and confirm SLA language, (4) Anna: sign off on thresholds and canary windows.
Anna P: will review thresholds and reply by noon.
Jordan (Eng): quick Q — do we want an A/B assignment algorithm pinned to user-id hash or random sample to ensure reproducibility? tenant-level routing uses sticky assignment at session start. recommend hash-based for deterministic split.
Tom (SE): hash-based for reproducibility + easier debugging. log assignment id in request headers: `X-AB-Cohort: priority-routing-canary`.
Rachel S (CS): I'll tell Acme the plan and ask for their preferred eval prompts. they'll likely ask for a private dashboard. can we give them read-only links?
Mike (ops): read-only dashboards OK for enterprise. I'll stub a Grafana board for the flag with panels: latency, errors, quality-delta, token-rate, ramp progress.
Sophia (PM): final check: rollback SLA 15m, telemetry retention 90d (billable), alert thresholds as above, warmup + autoscale, token cap. if everyone agrees I'll sign off and send the proposed runbook to Acme.
Anna P: agree.
Jordan (Eng): agree.
Tom (SE): agree.
Mike (ops): agree, will post cost estimate in the ticket.
Rachel S (CS): agree, will draft comms and ask for eval set.
Sophia (PM): thanks — I'll post the runbook & ship timeline once cost is confirmed. :thumbsup:
